subject: Request: moderation & external tool-call exemption — proposed ops guardrails
messages:
From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novopay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@novopay.com>, Novopay Legal <legal@novopay.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: External moderation/tool-call failures — request for SLA carveout language

Hi Sean,

Quick context: in our production rollout with Redwood we’re seeing intermittent increases in end-to-end latency when the third-party moderation layer or async tool-calls (payment verification webhook) are invoked. This isn’t a constant outage — more often a spike that pushes some requests past our 700ms SLO. Our procurement team is asking for explicit language acknowledging these failure modes and an exemption lane in the SLA that sets expectation for:

- What constitutes an "out-of-scope" failure (third-party moderation, vendor tool timeouts).
- A monitoring/alerting commitment from Redwood when these spikes cross thresholds.
- Whether we get retroactive credits for sustained regressions caused by these dependencies.

I’ve attached a short list of mitigation asks (novopay_mitigation_requirements.pdf). Can Redwood propose carveout wording plus suggested operational guardrails (runbook, escalation path, telemetry hooks)?

Thanks,
Alicia
Alicia Gomez
Head of Integrations, Novopay
---
Attachment: novopay_mitigation_requirements.pdf (PDF, 48KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novopay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: External moderation/tool-call failures — request for SLA carveout language

Alicia,

Appreciate the note and the doc — and thanks for laying out concrete asks. Looping in Lauren (Legal) and Marissa (Ops) so we can provide a combined legal + technical response and a proposed redline. High level: Redwood’s hosted SLA is for inference availability and per-token latency under standard routing. We do have precedent for narrowly-scoped carveouts where third-party moderation or customer-managed webhooks cause delays; what we want to avoid is broadly excluding any downstream dependency without compensating mitigations.

Quick questions to help us draft:
- Are the moderation calls you reference Redwood-managed (our moderation integration) or entirely Novopay-managed third-party calls?
- How frequently in your rollout did you observe >700ms spikes and for how long (sustained vs burst)?

We’ll aim to send a proposed redline + operational runbook by EOD tomorrow.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novopay.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: External moderation/tool-call failures — proposed ops guardrails

Sean / Lauren / Alicia,

Technical summary from Ops after looking at the logs Alicia shared:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of (1) occasionally slow responses from the external moderation vendor and (2) a small percentage of long-tail tool-call retries that stack with model generation.
- Impact: ~0.7% of requests in the window we examined exceeded 700ms; the 95th percentile remains <480ms.

Proposed operational guardrails (we’re attaching a draft runbook):
1) Explicit carveout scope: Redwood will declare as out-of-scope any latency caused exclusively by third-party moderation vendors or customer-owned webhooks invoked synchronously during token generation. We’ll add a definition and examples.
2) Monitoring commitment: Redwood will provide a dedicated telemetry dashboard and a webhook/alerting feed for Novopay that surfaces these dependency failures in near-real time (within 60s).
3) Mitigations: automatic async-fallback path — when a moderation call or tool-call exceeds 300ms, the request will route to a cached policy decision or to a safe-mode model variant that bypasses the external call to preserve latency. This preserves correctness for 95% of cases but may affect some structured-output fields (we’ll mark these in the API response).
4) Credits: For sustained regressions (>=72 hours where error/timeout rate >2% attributable to Redwood-managed moderation integration), Redwood will issue a pro-rated credit equivalent to the affected request volume. For customer-managed tools/third-party vendors we will assist with diagnostics but cannot extend automatic credits.
5) Rollout & testing: we propose a 2-week canary with Novopay traffic limits, followed by a 30-day validation window where both parties observe telemetry.

I’ve attached the runbook and the draft redline for legal. Happy to jump on a short call to finalize language.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Platform Operations — Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: moderation-fallback-runbook.pdf (PDF, 76KB); redwood-sla-redline-20270822.xlsx (Excel, 12KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novopay.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 13:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: External moderation/tool-call failures — proposed ops guardrails

Alicia,

Thanks for the quick follow-up and the Ops proposal — that’s very helpful. From Legal’s perspective we can accept the narrow carveout scope Marissa proposed with a couple of edits to tighten definitions and responsibilities:
- If Novopay elects Redwood’s managed moderation integration (i.e., where Redwood operates the moderation vendor link and controls retries), then the credit policy outlined by Marissa applies.
- If Novopay runs moderation or webhook calls in your own environment (you control the endpoint and authentication), Redwood will provide diagnostic correlation logs and a timeline but cannot take financial responsibility.
- We’ll add an SLA appendix language that requires both parties to run the 2-week canary and share raw telemetry for the 30-day validation window.

I’ve attached an updated redline (redwood-sla-redline-20270822.xlsx) with inline edits. If that looks ok, we can issue a DocuSign amendment for signature next week.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
---
Attachment: redwood-sla-redline-20270822.xlsx (Excel, updated)

From: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@novopay.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: External moderation/tool-call failures — proposed ops guardrails

Team,

Thanks — the proposed carveout language and the runbook align with what procurement needs. A couple practical items before we sign:
- Can Redwood confirm the exact telemetry fields you'll expose to our dashboard (we need per-request trace id, moderation vendor latency, tool-call latency, and fallback flag).
- We’d like the canary to begin next Tuesday (2027-08-31) to align with our release calendar.
- For the credits clause: Novopay requests a 14-day lookback window for Eligible Events (so we can request retroactive credits within that period).

If you can confirm those three items I’ll ask Legal to pre-approve the amendment and we’ll schedule signature.

Best,
Alicia
